body:
Tested e238560 on Linux with a GCC `target=template_release production=yes` build.
```
-rwxr-xr-x.  1 akien akien     75.16M Sep 29 21:18 godot.linuxbsd.template_release.x86_64.master
-rwxr-xr-x.  1 akien akien     74.69M Sep 29 21:40 godot.linuxbsd.template_release.x86_64.pr123984
```
So around 500 kB reduction "only", but that's still a pretty good gain.

No obvious performance impact on running a project and shutting it down:
```
$ hyperfine -w 5 -m 15 "time ./index.x86_64 --quit" "time ./index.x86_64pr --quit"
Benchmark 1: time ./index.x86_64 --quit
  Time (mean ± σ):     658.1 ms ±  21.7 ms    [User: 325.4 ms, System: 171.7 ms]
  Range (min … max):   613.9 ms … 713.7 ms    15 runs
 
Benchmark 2: time ./index.x86_64pr --quit
  Time (mean ± σ):     667.5 ms ±  25.8 ms    [User: 328.2 ms, System: 172.1 ms]
  Range (min … max):   642.6 ms … 715.0 ms    15 runs
 
Summary
  time ./index.x86_64 --quit ran
    1.01 ± 0.05 times faster than time ./index.x86_64pr --quit
~/.../build/web (main)$ hyperfine -w 5 -m 15 "time ./index.x86_64pr --quit" "time ./index.x86_64 --quit"
Benchmark 1: time ./index.x86_64pr --quit
  Time (mean ± σ):     662.5 ms ±  18.3 ms    [User: 330.1 ms, System: 170.1 ms]
  Range (min … max):   640.2 ms … 719.3 ms    15 runs
 
Benchmark 2: time ./index.x86_64 --quit
  Time (mean ± σ):     669.1 ms ±  14.3 ms    [User: 330.5 ms, System: 173.9 ms]
  Range (min … max):   650.9 ms … 709.7 ms    15 runs
 
Summary
  time ./index.x86_64pr --quit ran
    1.01 ± 0.04 times faster than time ./index.x86_64 --quit
```

*Edit:* I'll retest with the new commit.

```
-rwxr-xr-x.  1 akien akien     75.16M Sep 29 21:18 godot.linuxbsd.template_release.x86_64.master
-rwxr-xr-x.  1 akien akien     74.69M Sep 29 21:40 godot.linuxbsd.template_release.x86_64.pr123984
-rwxr-xr-x.  1 akien akien     74.58M Sep 29 21:56 godot.linuxbsd.template_release.x86_64.pr123984v2
```

With 8d7acc4 I now get 580 kB size reduction, or 0.8%.

Do we even need `configured`? The only thing it is used is for setting all elements of the array to `nullptr`, but static arrays are already zero initialized, like:
```C++
StringName::_Data *StringName::Table::table[TABLE_LEN];
```
Explanation (https://en.cppreference.com/cpp/language/zero_initialization):
> The effects of zero-initialization are:
> - If T is a [scalar type](https://en.cppreference.com/cpp/named_req/ScalarType), the object is initialized to the value obtained by [explicitly converting](https://en.cppreference.com/cpp/language/explicit_cast) the integer literal 0 (zero) to T.
> - ...
> - If T is array type, each element is zero-initialized.

Edit: Or I guess only leave it for `StringName::cleanup` and `StringName::unref` to stop error reporting? Hmm, the only thing that is truly needed is to detect when allocator is destructed and freed all its memory that can be checked inside the `StringName::unref`.

> Do we even need `configured`? The only thing it is used is for setting all elements of the array to `nullptr`, but static arrays are already zero initialized, like:
> 
> ```c++
> StringName::_Data *StringName::Table::table[TABLE_LEN];
> ```
> 
> Explanation (https://en.cppreference.com/cpp/language/zero_initialization):
> 
> > The effects of zero-initialization are:
> > 
> > * If T is a [scalar type](https://en.cppreference.com/cpp/named_req/ScalarType), the object is initialized to the value obtained by [explicitly converting](https://en.cppreference.com/cpp/language/explicit_cast) the integer literal 0 (zero) to T.
> > * ...
> > * If T is array type, each element is zero-initialized.
> 
> Edit: Or I guess only leave it for `StringName::cleanup` and `StringName::unref` to stop error reporting? Hmm, the only thing that is truly needed is to detect when allocator is destructed and freed all its memory that can be checked inside the `StringName::unref`.

`configured` is needed for shutdown. In `unref()` we can exit early if `!configured` (for e.g. static `StringName` instances); if we didn't have it we'd have to check for "`StringName` doesn't exist" and exit silently on `unref()` which might paper over some real bugs.
